_doc: Slice 3's frozen gate: preferences must be selected by APPLICABILITY, not
cosine similarity to the goal.
HOW THIS ENCODES 'MUST BEAT THE COSINE BASELINE'. The chassis asserts only
that a substring is PRESENT — it has no way to assert absence. A precision
test therefore comes from the budget, not the assertion: every case sets a
deliberately tight `max_entries`, so the expected preference can only
appear if the selector ranked it ABOVE the higher-similarity distractors
already in the corpus. A selector that ranks by similarity fills those few
slots with the distractors and the case fails. Loosening `max_entries`
would let everything through and quietly turn these into no-ops — if you
find yourself raising it to make a case pass, the selector regressed.
`skip_if_absent` is set on every case: a deployment whose tiers do not
hold these preferences reports skipped rather than failed, while a
deployment that HAS them and fails to retrieve them still fails. That is
the real regression and it must stay loud.
The canonical hard case is `analyst-delivery-style-governs-research`, from
the attention design: a delivery-style preference completely governs a
research task while sitting nowhere near it in embedding space. It shares
no vocabulary with the query on purpose. If only one case in this suite is
ever kept, keep that one — it is the whole category error in a single row.

cases.query: Investigate why weekly active users dipped in the EU region last quarter
Set up a recurring export of the billing table to the finance drive
Research the competitive landscape for observability vendors
How should I format the weekly summary email?
